title: DeepMind's AlphaEvolve runs in Google production, recovering 0.7% of worldwide compute with evaluator-verified code
summary: Google DeepMind's AlphaEvolve pairs Gemini Flash and Gemini Pro with automated evaluators that verify, run and score every candidate program, and an evolutionary loop over a programs database decides which candidates feed future prompts. Its outputs are in production at Google: a Borg scheduling heuristic deployed for over a year recovers on average 0.7% of Google's worldwide compute, a Verilog rewrite that had to pass functional-correctness verification was integrated into an upcoming TPU, and a 23% kernel speedup cut Gemini training time by 1%.
verification_note: URL fetched 2026-10-17. Page is the Google DeepMind blog post dated May 14, 2025. The 0.7% worldwide compute figure, over-a-year production of the Borg heuristic, the TPU Verilog change passing functional-correctness verification, and the 23% kernel speedup with 1% Gemini training-time reduction all appear in the page text. The page describes automated evaluator gating but no human review step or safety controls.
